venture.headline: Elorian Model Glimpse Outperforms GPT-6 Astra in Visual Reasoning Tasks
venture.summary: Elorian has introduced Glimpse, its first AI model designed to reason directly with images. According to internal evaluations, Glimpse outperforms GPT-6 Astra on scientific chart reasoning and short-form video captioning. The model also demonstrates competitive performance across other visual reasoning benchmarks.

venture.headline: Meta removes language that raised scraping and AI training concerns
venture.summary: A Meta spokesperson insisted that the updated terms did not reflect a change in the way Meta crawls the web.

research.headline: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
research.summary: Significant efforts are currently being directed toward the implementation of large-scale quantum information processors, but realizing useful quantum advantage also requires the development of efficient quantum algorithms. While for many practical problems the dominant resource costs are associated with a small set of computational primitives, optimizing them in the quantum setting presents unique challenges, including a reversibility constraint absent from ordinary classical computation. Here we introduce an evolutionary framework in which large language models (LLMs) propose circuit designs and an independent evaluator verifies and scores them.

research.headline: Open models have real benefits. Do they outweigh the risks?
research.summary: MIT Technology Review Explains: Let our writers untangle the complex, messy world of science and technology to help you understand what’s coming next. You can from the series here. Late last month, Anthropic released a report arguing that the model GLM-5.3 poses a major cyberattack risk.

research.headline: AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models
research.summary: When Keelan Miskell began winding down his crypto startup this year, he didn’t think its data was worth much: the users were anonymous, the company just a few years old. But he’s since turned the firm’s digital archives into real money. He’s netted roughly $25,000 for his code base and a still-pending amount (likely around….

research.headline: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
research.summary: Generative visual verifiers play a crucial role in advancing multimodal intelligence. To enhance the robustness of visual verifiers in complex multimodal scenarios involving compositional requirements, we move beyond conventional binary verifiers that produce only True/False discrete judgments and introduce a verifier that automatically decomposes complex prompts or environmental rules into fine-grained components and assigns pointwise scores to provide a continuous and more informative critique signal. Our experiments further demonstrate that these structured and interpretable outputs improve the verifier's generalization to out-of-domain multimodal critic tasks.

research.headline: Roundtables: A Conversation With the Creator of AI-Designed Viruses
research.summary: Listen to the session or watch below Can AI design new life forms? In 2025, Stanford University PhD student Samuel King came up with a preliminary answer when he used a generative AI model to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses. It isn’t yet an example of AI-generated life, but that could be next.

titans.headline: Meta removes language that may have allowed it to scrape news sites
titans.summary: After backlash, Meta is updating its terms again to remove language that suggested it could scrape content from sites, including news sites, to train its AI. Specifically, the following language no longer appears on the commercial terms page: … Meta may use any content from such domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, […].

titans.headline: A week with RTX Spark: everything we’ve learned using Nvidia’s new laptops
titans.summary: Nvidia's RTX Spark N1X processor is finally here, and we've been collectively testing a small fortune's worth of powerful laptops sporting this new "superchip." RTX Spark is designed to be a high-performing Arm-based SoC for laptops and small desktop computers, rivaling the best from Apple, Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm. It has loads of cores, Nvidia […].

titans.headline: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
titans.summary: Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes. But what happens when the rest of the internet won't play nice?

titans.headline: Meta’s new terms may allow it to train AI on news sites for free
titans.summary: Meta's new terms appear to give it permission to crawl and scrape websites "associated" with the businesses that use its platforms - including online publishers, according to a report from Nieman Lab. The new terms, which go into effect on October 30th, say Meta can use this outside content to "develop, improve, research," and "train" […].

titans.headline: ChatGPT can peek at your Chrome tabs now
titans.summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT Atlas browser is gone, but now ChatGPT's Google Chrome extension is getting some upgrades that allow it to use the browser tabs you already have open. With the extension installed, OpenAI says ChatGPT can now view your browser tabs when you tag Chrome in ChatGPT's web or desktop app, posting a demo video […].

regulatory.headline: FTC Sends $9.8 Million to Consumers Harmed by Walmart Wire Transfer Scams
regulatory.summary: The Federal Trade Commission is issuing over $9.8 million in payments to affected consumers. The refunds follow Walmart's alleged failure to stop scammers from misusing its wire transfer services. Scammers previously extracted hundreds of millions of dollars from U.S. customers through the company's money transfer platform.

regulatory.headline: FTC Sues REPS & Company For Illegally Bypassing Ticket Limits
regulatory.summary: The Federal Trade Commission sued REPS & Company Inc. for allegedly circumventing ticket purchasing limits. According to the complaint, the broker unlawfully bypassed security measures to buy millions of event tickets that it resold at a significant profit.

regulatory.headline: FTC Sues Digital Forensics Corporation Over Alleged Sextortion Scheme
regulatory.summary: A federal court temporarily halted operations for Digital Forensics Corporation LLC and its CEO following an FTC lawsuit. The FTC alleges the company defrauded consumers out of millions by promising to identify criminals and end sextortion attacks while charging thousands of dollars without providing services. Additionally, the company is accused of engaging in deceptive review practices.

frontier.headline: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope exceeds expectations by nearly 30%
frontier.summary: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has exceeded expectations after engineers made incredibly tiny adjustments to sharpen its view of the universe. By moving a mirror just one-sixteenth the width of a human hair, the team helped bring its powerful instruments into near-perfect alignment. Roman’s Wide Field Instrument now produces image quality nearly 30% better than predicted, promising exceptionally sharp cosmic surveys.

frontier.headline: Magna: simulating magic state factories as cheaply as Clifford circuits
frontier.summary: Classical simulation of magic state factories, including distillation, cultivation, and code switching, is challenging because of their substantial non-Clifford content. We introduce $\texttt{magna}$ (magic-state-factory assessment via global network algebra), a classical simulator that simulates such protocols as cheaply as Clifford circuits. $\texttt{magna}$ expresses the figures of merit of a protocol, namely the acceptance rate and the fidelity of the accepted states, as tensor networks, which it reduces globally by exploiting a structural correspondence with transversal gates on quantum codes.

frontier.headline: Stability of Quantum LDPC States under Local Pauli Noise
frontier.summary: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes have a canonical mixed state---the normalized projector onto the code space---that lies at the intersection of quantum error correction and quantum many-body physics, yet the stability of its information-theoretic structure under local noise remains poorly understood. Recent progress on mixed-state phases of matter has identified the spatial decay of conditional mutual information (CMI) $I(A:C|B)$ as a key diagnostic of such stability, analogous to the role of the spectral gap for quantum ground states. We prove that, for the normalized code-projector state of a $\mathbb{Z}_d$ qLDPC stabilizer code under local Pauli noise, the CMI across a buffer $B$ separating $A$ from $C$ decays exponentially with the width of $B$ in two complementary noise regimes independent of system size.

industry.headline: The New Fan’s Guide to the Unreal World of Nathan Fielder
industry.summary: Surprised by the hype around yet another documentary on Theranos fraudster Elizabeth Holmes? It has everything to do with this experimental comedian.

industry.headline: Alex Gibney’s ‘Musk’ Has a Unique Perspective on Daddy Issues
industry.summary: Elon Musk’s father, Errol Musk, agreed to be interviewed immediately.

voices.headline: Courts Block Trump DOJ Attempts to Obtain State Voter Rolls
voices.summary: The Department of Justice filed lawsuits against 30 states and the District of Columbia to force the surrender of sensitive state voter information to federal authorities. Federal judges across the political spectrum rejected the administration's demands in 26 district court cases, citing a lack of legal authorization. The rulings highlight how America's decentralized election system and the courts limit federal attempts to control state voter rolls.

voices.headline: Lawmaker Proposes Advanced AI Ban to Stop Tech Oligarchs From Replacing Humans
voices.summary: Tech industry leaders like Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and Peter Thiel advocate transhumanist visions that view artificial intelligence as a successor or merge-partner to humanity. In response to public concern over these initiatives, lawmakers introduced legislation to pause advanced AI development and ban artificial superintelligence. The proposed bill seeks to establish a new federal body to ensure safety before development resumes.

voices.headline: The Final Defenders
voices.summary: For the first time in her career, Cynthia Short let a folder of crime-scene photographs lie untouched on the corner of her desk, because she couldn’t bring herself to look at them. Short had been a criminal-defense attorney in Kansas City, Missouri, for 12 years, and on the payroll of the Missouri State Public Defender’s Office for the past decade. She had spent much of that time immersed in graphic records of the worst human conduct.

voices.headline: What Newsrooms Should Know Before They Take Money From OpenAI
voices.summary: As a newsroom executive, I have long tried to resist appeals to vet donors to nonprofit journalism for their politics or even the savoriness of their business practices. When you do that, you raise questions about whether you could fairly cover any potential donors on your banned list, and you also run the risk of offering some sort of implicit endorsement to the rest. Both of those perceptions are antithetical to the independent stance that good journalism requires.

voices.headline: Invasion of the Self-Replicating AI-Malware Botnet
voices.summary: Have you ever counted the computers in your house? You’re probably including your desktop and laptop computers, if you own some. I bet you’re also including the smartphones and tablets.
